content:
Connor O'Brien: Heads up, cherry-pick into `runtime-1.18-lts` is stuck on a nasty conflict. It’s the starvation backport (PR-23457) on top of the batching heuristic disable (PR-23366). Anyone around to help untangle? Need this for 1.18.1-lts RC.

Devon Price: yep, saw the bot open the backport PR and then fail. Paste the conflict chunk?

Connor O'Brien: from the backport branch:
```
$ git cherry-pick -x 3f2a1b7c1e  # upstream commit for 23457
Auto-merging runtime/scheduler/queue_policy.cc
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in runtime/scheduler/queue_policy.cc
Auto-merging runtime/config/runtime_defaults.yaml
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in runtime/config/runtime_defaults.yaml
error: could not apply 3f2a1b7c1e... scheduler: mitigate starvation under bursty traffic
```

Sofia Ivanova: I can take. That file moved around slightly in LTS when we guarded experimental batching. Likely conflict is just the new `min_fair_share_tokens` default + the old heuristic toggle.

Hiro Tanaka: :eyes: also note LTS froze autotune params (PR-23241). There was a rename in defaults yaml around the same time.

Sahana Iyer: FYI release branch CI will treat defaults changes as “config surface change” and require the `release-config-ack` label. Not blocking if we keep it minimal.

Noah Patel: if it’s touching defaults, we should be careful. For LTS we probably want the starvation fix without changing unrelated tuning knobs.

Connor O'Brien: agreed. Goal: include starvation fix logic + its regression test, but avoid changing unrelated defaults unless required for correctness.

Sofia Ivanova: ok, opening the conflict locally. In `queue_policy.cc` upstream added `effective_weight = max(weight, kMinWeight)` but LTS has extra guard paths for `experimental_batching_enabled`.

Sofia Ivanova: likely resolution: keep LTS guard rails, but insert starvation mitigation inside the “normal” path only. The test should still pass.

Devon Price: if you want, I can prep a tiny “resolution notes” blurb for the next patch checklist. This conflict feels repeatable.

Leila Farouk: once resolved, please ping me — I’ll run the scheduler smoke suite on the backport PR (the mixed prompt lengths test is the one that caught this originally).

Sofia Ivanova: found conflict region. Here’s what upstream wants:
```
// upstream
if (queue_backlog_ms > kStarvationBacklogMs) {
  boost_low_priority = true;
}
```
In LTS we have:
```
if (experimental_batching_enabled) {
  // old heuristic path
  ...
} else {
  // stable path
  ...
}
```
I propose placing the backlog check in the stable path only, plus keeping the existing LTS gating. That keeps semantics aligned with “experimental batching disabled” on LTS.

Noah Patel: +1. If experimental is off, the fix is active; if someone overrides and turns it on, they’re already outside the LTS “predictable” envelope.

Connor O'Brien: :thumbsup: works for me. What about `runtime_defaults.yaml` conflict?

Sofia Ivanova: that’s mostly key rename. Upstream added:
`runtime.scheduler.starvation_backlog_ms: 250`
But LTS defaults file moved to:
`runtime.scheduler.backpressure.starvation_backlog_ms` (because of the batching disable refactor). I think we should:
- keep the LTS namespacing (backpressure.*)
- add the new key under that namespace
- do NOT change the actual numeric defaults beyond adding the key

Hiro Tanaka: please double-check it doesn’t collide with kernel autotune defaults section — last time we hit a YAML conflict because someone re-ordered keys.

Sahana Iyer: reordering causes a bunch of noisy diffs + makes future cherry-picks worse. Prefer minimal diff: insert line exactly where it fits in the existing block.

Devon Price: also, our cherry-pick helper currently does `--strategy=ort` default, which sometimes reorders conflict markers in YAML in weird ways. We should capture a “don’t auto-format YAML on release branch” note.

Connor O'Brien: ok. Sofia, can you push your resolved version to the backport PR? I’ll stay on for review.

Sofia Ivanova: yep. Doing:
```
$ git checkout backport/23457-runtime-1.18-lts
# resolve files
$ git add runtime/scheduler/queue_policy.cc runtime/config/runtime_defaults.yaml
$ git cherry-pick --continue
```

GitHub Actions: CI run queued for backport/23457-runtime-1.18-lts (release-branch workflow)

Sofia Ivanova: pushed. Backport PR updated with conflict resolution commit message “Resolve conflicts with LTS batching guard rails”. Link: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/23457 (backport)

Connor O'Brien: reviewing now. In `queue_policy.cc` I see:
- starvation backlog check only in stable path
- added comment: “LTS: experimental batching path not covered by starvation mitigation”
Looks fine.

Leila Farouk: pulling branch and running scheduler suite now.

Sahana Iyer: CI note: you touched defaults yaml; please add `release-config-ack` label to the PR or it’ll fail the “config review required” gate.

Connor O'Brien: added label.

Devon Price: while we wait, can we document “how to avoid next patch” here?

Connor O'Brien: yes, please. This one burned an hour.

Devon Price: proposal for runbook / checklist addition:
1) When backporting scheduler fixes that touch defaults, cherry-pick in this order on LTS:
   a) config namespace/guard PRs (e.g., experimental batching disable)
   b) then functional fix PRs (starvation)
2) Do not run YAML formatters on release branches; keep diffs minimal to reduce conflict probability.
3) If conflict in `runtime_defaults.yaml`, preserve LTS key namespaces (don’t “re-align” to mainline) and add compatibility comments.
4) Add `release-config-ack` label when defaults change; ping Sahana for quick approval.

Sofia Ivanova: + add note: “If the upstream fix assumes experimental batching on, re-evaluate whether it should be active under LTS settings; prefer applying only to stable path.”

Noah Patel: also: when resolving conflict, avoid changing behavior by merging both sides. Pick LTS behavior + surgically insert the fix, then add a regression test reference in the PR body.

Hiro Tanaka: and avoid reordering YAML blocks. keep key order stable.

Connor O'Brien: great. Devon can you drop that into the PR description and I’ll also paste into the release manager checklist repo after this patch.

Devon Price: will do.

Leila Farouk: scheduler smoke suite results:
- `scheduler_overload_backpressure_test` ✅
- `mixed_prompt_lengths_fairness` ✅
- new reproducer for starvation ✅
No flakes on my run.

GitHub Actions: release-branch workflow succeeded for backport/23457-runtime-1.18-lts

Sahana Iyer: perf-canary is still required before merging, but from CI side looks good.

Connor O'Brien: perf canary scheduled. Thanks all. I’m going to summarize the conflict + resolution in-thread so we can link it next time:
- Conflict root cause: mainline PR introduced starvation mitigation + new defaults key; LTS had prior refactor to disable experimental batching + rename config namespaces.
- Resolution: keep LTS guard rails; apply mitigation only to stable scheduling path; add new defaults key under existing LTS namespace; minimal diff/no reformat.

Connor O'Brien: Action item: Devon to add “avoid YAML reformat + backport order + stable-path-only guidance” to runbook/checklist. Sofia/Leila: thanks for jumping in.

Devon Price: noted. Will PR the checklist update after 1.18.1-lts cuts so we don’t risk merge noise during RC. :thumbsup:
